ANSWER: The function that decides whether a piece of text looks like a secret is **`secret_kind`** in `src/memory/guard.rs` (line 53). It first checks the text against a set of named regex patterns (private keys, AWS keys, GitHub tokens, JWTs, etc.). If none match, it scans for any token of 32+ mixed characters using the `LONG_TOKEN` regex, then calls the helper **`looks_random`** (line 62, same file) on each match. `looks_random` distinguishes high-entropy base64-style tokens from hex hashes and IDs by requiring that the token contain lowercase letters, uppercase letters, and digits simultaneously, then computing Shannon entropy — tokens above 4.2 bits/character are flagged as `"high-entropy token"`. Hex/base32 strings fail because they lack mixed case, and simple IDs fail the entropy threshold.

CONFIDENCE: high
